title: Non-raising forms: `strict=False` and `wrap_numerical`
verdict: `strict=False` gives NULL for an invalid cast; `wrap_numerical` wraps
description: `cast(strict=False)` gives NULL where the cast is invalid; `wrap_numerical=True` wraps overflowing numeric casts instead of marking them invalid (`cast` page). The probes confirm both for integer and double casts (polars-cast-int, polars-cast-double-to-int) and strict parsing for strings (polars-cast-string).

Polars has no general `TRY(expr)`. String parsers (`str.to_integer`, `str.strptime`, `str.to_date`) take their own `strict` flag; which errors they turn into NULL, and whether a non-strict cast of nested types nulls the field or the row, goes to source and tests (py-polars/tests/unit/operations/test_cast.py: `test_nested_strict_casts_failing`, `test_strict_cast_nested`).
reference: Substrait's cast has `failure_behavior: RETURN_NULL`; the reference honours it on DuckDB only, and other engines refuse it until #271 (`docs/reference-semantics.md`).
